questions.text: Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) about the Transformer encoder. Assertion (A): In a Transformer encoder, each token can attend to every other token in the input sequence through self-attention. Reason (R): The encoder's self-attention mechanism uses a causal mask to prevent each token from attending to tokens that appear later in the sequence. Choose the correct option:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.correct_answer: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.text: You are designing an LLM to translate a sentence from English to Spanish with low computational complexity. The system has to consider a few possible sequences of words rather than committing to the single highest-probability word at every step. Which of the following decoding strategies is the most appropriate?
options: Beam search
Exhaustive search
Top-p sampling with p = 0.85
Greedy decoding

questions.text: In the Next Sentence Prediction task, how are the two input sentences distinguished by the BERT architecture?
options: By utilizing separate transformer encoders for each sentence and concatenating the outputs.
By adding learnable segment embeddings to the token and positional embeddings of the respective sentences.
By inserting a [MASK] token between the two sentences.
By ensuring two different heads in the Multi-Head Attention setup attend to the specific sentences.
questions.correct_answer: By adding learnable segment embeddings to the token and positional embeddings of the respective sentences.

questions.text: How did the GPT-2 model initially demonstrate "zero-shot domain transfer" capabilities on complex tasks like summarization and translation?
options: By utilizing specialized adapter layers trained explicitly for translation and summarization datasets.
By formatting the raw input text with natural language prompts to induce task-specific outputs without updating model weights.
By executing a secondary pre-training phase exclusively on Wikipedia and BookCorpus.
By modifying the decoder architecture into a bidirectional encoder for specific tasks.
questions.correct_answer: By formatting the raw input text with natural language prompts to induce task-specific outputs without updating model weights.

Which of the following statements about length generalization in Large Language Models (LLMs) are correct?
options: Length generalization is the ability of an LLM to maintain effective performance on sequences longer than the sequence lengths predominantly used during training.
Length generalization refers specifically to improving computational efficiency when processing longer sequences.
Length generalization can depend on the model architecture, positional encoding scheme, training procedure, and the nature of the task.
Exposure to a wider range of sequence lengths during training can improve an LLM's ability to generalize to longer sequences.
correct_answer: Length generalization is the ability of an LLM to maintain effective performance on sequences longer than the sequence lengths predominantly used during training.
Length generalization can depend on the model architecture, positional encoding scheme, training procedure, and the nature of the task.
Exposure to a wider range of sequence lengths during training can improve an LLM's ability to generalize to longer sequences.
